characteristic.rule: Read only after CameraManager returns CameraCharacteristics for the named camera ID.

session.rule: Apply only as a session parameter before createCaptureSession; changing it requires session recreation unless a target trace proves otherwise.

request.rule: Apply to the intended CaptureRequest.Builder after template creation and before build or submission.

physical-request.rule: Apply only through a physical-camera request path for the named physical ID; ordinary logical-camera use is unsupported until verified.

result.rule: Read only from the matching CaptureResult or TotalCaptureResult after result delivery.

failureTaxonomy.description: The Java/native metadata type or array shape does not match the target implementation.
The value is rejected, clamped, ignored or outside the advertised target-build domain.
A session-scoped key or incompatible stream combination prevents session configuration.
The framework, service or HAL rejects a request containing the key.
Metadata is accepted but no effective image-pipeline or routing change is measured.
The camera device disconnects, errors, stalls or exceeds the guarded probe timeout.

interpretationRules: Every materialized vendor-tag record must have explicit type, value, ordering, dependency, effect, error, build-scope and safety fields even when the value is UNKNOWN.
Advertisement in CameraCharacteristics is read evidence only and never proves that an ordinary application may write a key.
Public MediaTek source matches are PARTIALLY_VERIFIED hints until the target firmware metadata or matching target binary confirms them.
Candidate routing objectives remain HYPOTHESIS until a one-variable target-device probe measures a causal effect.
No key may expose write sample configuration unless its type, value, effect, rollback and exact-build scope are VERIFIED.
Unsupported or unknown writes must remain disabled and must name the public Camera2 fallback.
